messages:
Maya: FYI paging: customer cluster in eu-west has sustained GPU queue growth for ~22m, hitting capacity limits and failing autoscale. Customers reporting 503s.

oncall-bot: Incident created — SEV: high. PagerDuty alert sent to rotation. Thread TS=2555554321

Owen: Jumping in. Which customer? any specific constraints?

Maya: acme-tech. Private VPC, node pool max 8 gpus, autoscaler is trying to spin new nodes but provisioning stays Pending for minutes. Logs show long image pulls and ENI attach retries.

Samir: Seen similar before when cloud account had strict ENI rate limits + a custom AMI that pulls a lot at boot. Can we check node provisioning logs and kube events?

Li-Chen: I pulled controller-manager and cloud-provider logs. Key lines: ```
I0313 12:34:21.123 kubelet: pulling image redwood/gpu-runtime:2026-03-10
I0313 12:34:58.432 cloud: attach ENI failed: rateLimited
I0313 12:35:10.002 autoscaler: scale up request for 3 nodes -> pending
```

Maya: Also seeing repeated kube-scheduler backoffs: pods stuck in ContainerCreating.

Ops-Eng: Quick customer impact summary: ~40% of inference requests hitting queue -> 503s for 30% of pods. Latency spikes for streaming. Customer report started ~12:10 UTC, impact ongoing.

pagerduty-bot: Pager acknowledged by Owen. ETA for first mitigation 12:45 UTC.

Owen: Mitigation plan: 1) temporarily raise node pool max to 12 (if allowed), 2) if cloud quotas block, open fallback: start warm fallback pool in a different AZ with pre-baked minimal image, 3) throttle low-priority jobs, 4) notify customer with estimated ETA. Thoughts?

Samir: +1. Check quota limits before bumping max. If the AMI pull is the bottleneck we should launch nodes with baked image (no heavy init). I can spawn a prebaked image in a warm pool.

Li-Chen: Quota check: current ENI attach quota near limit in eu-west-1 for this account. Cloud console shows 2 pending ENI attachments. If we scale beyond quota, attaches will queue and nodes remain NotReady.

Maya: Trying soft mitigation: throttling lower-priority batch routes at the ingress level (50% reduction) to reduce token pressure. Applying rate-limit rule now.

Maya: /cmd kubectl annotate nodepool acme-gpu max=12  -- dry-run shows server accepts change (no immediate error). Proceed?

Owen: Proceed only after Samir confirms fallback warm pool. Also open a support ticket with provider for ENI limit spike and request temporary quota bump. Samir — can you put up the fallback?

Samir: Spinning fallback pool in eu-west-b with prebaked runtime image. Using runbook snippet: ```bash
# create warm nodes
redwood ctl nodepool create --name acme-warm-b --gpus 4 --image baked-gpu-2026-03-05 --az eu-west-1b --min 2 --max 2
```
Starting now.

Li-Chen: Noted: adding autoscaler policy change to prefer POD selectors with high-priority label to existing nodes first. Applying rollout to avoid thrash.

Maya: Customer notified: "We are seeing degraded inference performance due to node provisioning delays. Mitigations in progress, ETA ~30m. Will update"

Ops-Eng: Monitoring: queue length peaked 92k token-requests, now down to 56k after throttle. 503 rate trending down from 30% -> 18%.

Samir: Fallback pool nodes moved to Ready at 12:53 UTC, routing rule added to steer overflow to warm pool. Initial traffic shift shows latency stable but reduced 503s.

Owen: After-action immediate items: - Confirm quota ticket + cloud support case number - Bake AMI with minimal runtime and keep 2 warm nodes for this customer - Add autoscaler policy to detect ENI attach failures and fall back sooner.

Maya: Logging next steps into incident tracker. Will keep thread updated. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring. If regression, reopen.

Maya: I'll handoff to oncall at 13:15 UTC for monitoring window. Owen — can you own postmortem?

Owen: Happy to. Will collect timelines and customer impact, draft postmortem and recommendations.

oncall-bot: Handoff noted: monitoring until 14:15 UTC.

Maya: Closing thread for active mitigation; leave comments if you find anything else.
